In the usual (monopole-free) Maxwell equations we have  

1. ∇·E = ρe/ε0                      (Gauss for E)  
2. ∇·B = 0                          (Gauss for B)  
3. ∇×E = –∂B/∂t                    (Faraday’s law)  
4. ∇×B = μ0J + μ0ε0 ∂E/∂t    (Ampère–Maxwell)

Introduce magnetic charge density ρm and magnetic current density Jm.  
The divergence of B can no longer be zero; it must equal the magnetic charge
density (up to constants).  To keep the equations self-consistent (take the divergence
of the curl equation and use the continuity equation
∂ρm/∂t + ∇·Jm = 0), Faraday’s law must also acquire an extra term involving Jm.
The modified pair is therefore  

∇·B = μ0 ρm             (non-zero flux of B)  
∇×E = –∂B/∂t – μ0 Jm    (curl/circulation of E altered)

The other two equations—Gauss’s law for E and the Ampère–Maxwell law—stay exactly the same.

Hence the equations that change are the one for the divergence of B and the one for the circulation (curl) of E.

Answer: B
